title: Coraline — Meaning, Genes, And Nothing Else #Shorts
description:
The genes do not care about Coraline; they care about copies. Coraline () is a 2002 British fantasy horror children's novella by author Neil Gaiman. Gaiman started writing Coraline in 1990, and it was published in 2002 by Bloomsbury and HarperCollins.

Modern psychology keeps rediscovering what the pessimists said first about Coraline. In his study of the novella, David Rudd argues that the work plays and riffs productively on Sigmund Freud's concept of Unheimlich ("the Uncanny"). Craig Russell, lettered by Todd Klein and colored by Lovern Kindzierski, was published in 2008.
